title: SELECT * vs only the needed columns
claim: SELECT * transfers more data and prevents covering indexes: with only indexed columns the database can
answer from the index without touching the table.
verdict: Partly confirmed, with a delayed side effect. **SELECT * has a delayed side effect that no test can catch when
the code is written: its cost depends on columns that do not exist yet. When a column is added to the table
later, for example a large text or JSON field, every SELECT * starts reading, transferring and decoding it and
gets slower, without any change to the query and without a new deployment of the code that runs it.** Sending
all columns of 96k rows took {x:star_client/columns_client} longer than 4 columns (rows average 203 vs 83
bytes). The bigger win is the covering effect: with only indexed columns the query became an Index Only Scan,
pages instead of {pages:star_index}. metric rows are narrow; with large responsebody values the transfer gap

SELECT pg_size_pretty(pg_table_size('sc_wide')) AS table_incl_toast,

       round(avg(length(details))) AS avg_details_chars
  FROM sc_wide;
